correctness.rationale: For the unique two-cycle, x+y=1-d follows by telescoping logit h(f(t))-h(t)=a(t-b). Exact cycle equation x=[(1-x)(1-d-x)/(d+x)] exp[-a((1-d)/2-x)] gives x~(1-d)d^-1 exp(-1/d) at both nearby parameters using uniform endpoint bounds of the earlier Oct11 theorem. Exact multiplier (1-aq(x))(1-aq(y)) expands to 1+Lambda=-d(1-d)Delta_a+4x/(1-d)+o(x) uniformly for the two exponentially close parameters; neutral condition yields constant4 and comparison sign. Independent high precision values d=.12,.08,.05,.035 converge to normalized constants.

The explicit sign and normalized prefactor answer a natural singular-bifurcation question, motivated by a known previously unresolved threshold.

final_claim: For f_a,b(t)=t/[t+(1-t)exp(a(t-b))] and b=(1-d)/2 with d downarrow0, the unique period-two neutral-flip boundary has d^2 exp(1/d)(a_f-2/[d(1-d)]) ->4, and its smaller orbit endpoint satisfies d exp(1/d)x_f/(1-d)->1. At the rational comparison coupling d exp(1/d)(1+Lambda_rat)/4->1, so that coupling is strictly attracting for small d.
